newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends down sharply, March at 7-month low.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends down sharply, March at 7-month low.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures plummeted to their lowest level in more than seven months on Tuesday, battered by heavy speculative selling, trading sources said.
Traders said frustration over the market's lackluster performance on Monday, combined with weakness in the London cocoa market, sparked a wave of chart-driven selling.
"The market was disappointed by the weak close yesterday," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "London hitting new lows accelerated the losses."
In New York, most-active March cocoa tumbled $32 a tonne on the day, to $1,351, its lowest settlement since late March, after ranging narrowly between $1,383 and $1,350.
Spot December, which goes into notice period Thursday, also fell $32, to $1,305. Open interest in December stood at 9,646 lots as of Monday, down 1,063 lots from the previous session.
London's LIFFE futures also fell to fresh seven-month lows Tuesday, with key March delivery ending at 925 stg.
Traders said light scale-down manufacturer buying absorbed some of the selling and prevented March from breaching support at $1,350.
Although fresh fundamentals have been scarce so far this week, analysts said a growing consensus that the 1996/97 cocoa yield would surpass early expectations was weighing on futures prices.
Technically, traders continued to peg March support near the $1,350 level, with the next downside target seen at $1,335. Resistance was put at $1,365.
Turnover was brisk, at an estimated 17,865 lots.
